# WO-614: Removal that does not need a search: send requests to blocked sites without a listing URL where the site allows it
Status: queued (in-house)
Vendor: claude
Agent: broker-researcher (Priya Shah) then automation-engineer (Theo Park)
Kind: research
Tier: deep
Severity: HIGH
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Target release: 0.4
Source: owner direction 2026-11-11 ("find a way to fully automate"), after WO-601 showed every people-search page blocks a cloud fetch. PII-free by rule.
Boundary (all WOs 612-616): shared rule 5 stands. No CAPTCHA solving, no stealth plugins, no solver services, no UA or fingerprint spoofing, no proxies or IP rotation. "Fully automated" here means: the app does every step a machine may do, from the person's own computer, and asks the person only for the one click a site reserves for humans, batched so it happens rarely.

## Goal
A blocked search must not block removal. Many brokers accept a deletion request by email or form with name + address only, or are covered by a parent company's single opt-out (Mississippi Tornado Alley LLC runs 5 of the WO-601 sites). For those, Free My ID should send the request directly (Email tier) and say "not checked, we asked anyway" (WO-602 wording).

## Tasks
- [ ] 1. Priya: for each of the 20 WO-601 brokers, record `optout_needs_listing_url` (true/false) and `optout_parent` with citations; group sites sharing one opt-out.
- [ ] 2. Orchestrator: add the two fields to the Broker model + schema (contract).
- [ ] 3. Theo: runner sends the search-free request for presumed sites where `optout_needs_listing_url` is false, once per parent group; data minimisation (rule 6) unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Registry validates with the new fields; every value has a citation.
2. Runner test: blocked-search broker with `optout_needs_listing_url: false` gets one request; with `true` gets a hand-check to-do; a parent group gets one request, not five.
